value: circadian clock is set through phytochrome: mutants in phytochrome A and in phytochromobilin synthase (phytochrome chromophore) have a shorter circadian period of cotyledon movement than wild type
method: abstract read on the publisher page (MDPI) through a page summary; mutant lines from a TILLING population, cotyledon movement recorded as circadian rhythm

source.authors: Perez-Santangelo S, Napier N, Robson F, Weller JL, Bond DM, Macknight RC
source.title: A Point Mutation in Phytochromobilin synthase Alters the Circadian Clock and Photoperiodic Flowering of Medicago truncatula

where: Abstract; the sentence is given by the page summary in two consecutive pieces joined here
quote: The analysis of the circadian clock in the MtpΦbs mutant revealed a shorter circadian period, which was shared with the MtphyA mutant.
note: Read through a page summary of the abstract; the full text was not opened. The summary reported Results periods of about 23.8 h (mutant) and 26.7 h (wild type) but these were not checked against the text and are not recorded.

source.authors: Gao Q, Hu S, Wang X, Han F, Luo H, Liu Z, Kang C
source.title: The red/far-red light photoreceptor FvePhyB regulates tissue elongation and anthocyanin accumulation in woodland strawberry

where: Abstract, two consecutive lines joined into one sentence
quote: The light treatment assay revealed that FvePhyB is a bona fide red/far-red light photoreceptor, as it specifically inhibits hypocotyl length under red light.
note: Read from the abstract only, through a page summary; the full text was not opened. Journal issue (10, 12) from the summary.

value: reads day length through phytochrome A: antisense reduction of the endogenous PHYA gene shifts photoperiodic requirements, giving earlier growth cessation and bud formation as days shorten
method: abstract read on the publisher page (Springer) through a page summary; transgenic hybrid aspen with antisense PttPHYA
conditions: daylength shortening; hybrid aspen (PttPHYA is the hybrid's phytochrome A gene)

source.authors: Kozarewa I, Ibanez C, Johansson M, Ogren E, Mozley D, Nylander E, Chono M, Moritz T, et al.
source.title: Alteration of PHYA expression change circadian rhythms and timing of bud set in Populus

where: Abstract; quote cut at 'shortening' (the sentence may continue after it)
quote: The antisense plants showed altered photoperiodic requirements, resulting in earlier growth cessation and bud formation in response to daylength shortening
note: Read from the abstract only, through a page summary that paraphrased most of it; the hybrid (not a species) was measured, so the grade is g for the genus. Authors: nine are listed on the page, shown here as the first eight and et al. The full text was not opened.
